# Developer Journal — 2026-08-24

## Summary

This cycle was about **UX polish and security hardening** across the ecosystem. The standout work is dominion-tracker's bigpicture feature — a full builds browser with interactive UI patterns (cover-flow launcher, spring physics, parallax). Security work landed in socialChat (hardcoded credential removal), robustness fixes in turbolab (llama-server recovery), and new CLI scripting support in cde-wallpaper. The pattern across repos: shipping interactive features while tightening the edges around credentials and system resilience.

## Per-Repo Activity

### turbolab
Hardened the llama-server startup path with detection for broken installations and automatic re-install logic in the process manager. Small change, high signal — the kind of thing that prevents user support spirals.

### cde-wallpaper
Added a CLI interface for scripting, unlocking programmatic use. Moves the project from UI-only to composable-in-shell territory, which fits the broader "binaries as building blocks" philosophy.

### socialChat
Removed hardcoded passwords from bot accounts and made bot authentication non-loggable. Security-first win: bots can't be compromised through log exfiltration, and no credentials sit in source as a ticking clock.

### dominion-tracker
The heavy lift this cycle. Built out a full builds browser (bigpicture) with a cover-flow launcher, color-coded builds by type, remote-friendly build creator, and interactive elements (clickable backs, game cancel, local date handling, player bios). The UI layer added spring physics and parallax parallax ambient effects — responsive but not gratuitous, suggesting careful attention to the interaction model. The feature set is vertical: you can now explore, create, and navigate builds in a discoverable UI instead of being stuck in tabular views.

### vitalSVG
Introduced a monitor-ring logo and propagated it through header, favicon, and docs. Branding coherence — small surface area but clarifies visual identity.

# Developer Journal — 2026-08-24

## Summary

Three repos shipped meaningful features this cycle. Blopple reached a milestone with standalone HTML export — the editor can now generate self-contained playable games in a single file, complete with fullscreen and aspect-preserving canvas scaling. Turbolab gained reasoning capabilities through chain-of-thought prompting and self-consistency sampling, letting the LLM server generate multiple candidate outputs and select the most consistent. omniMux picked up a defensive fix for malformed track metadata from yt-dlp. The throughline: rounding out feature sets (export pipeline, reasoning, robustness) rather than chasing new territory.

## Per-Repo Activity

### Blopple

The export pipeline shipped: standalone HTML generation with fullscreen support and aspect-ratio preservation, backed by a recently-saves list and export modal. Simultaneously invested in editor quality-of-life — undo/redo now covers both tilemap and texture pixel edits. Caught and fixed a texture orientation bug in wall/riser rendering, and squeezed two performance wins (canvas alpha context, hoisted plane distance math out of the inner column loop).

### turbolab

Added configurable default system prompts to the inference server, then went deeper with chain-of-thought reasoning: the server can now sample multiple model outputs, score them for internal consistency, and surface the best candidate. A dev-mode viewer lets you inspect what the model considered. Tests cover both the CoT logic and the endpoint integration.

### omniMux

Hardened metadata parsing: yt-dlp sometimes emits non-numeric track numbers, which was crashing tag writes. Now guards the tracknumber field with a type check before storing it.

# Developer Journal — 2026-08-14 through 2026-08-24

## Summary

A productive two weeks across the portfolio split between UX polish (omniMux), test expansion (Blopple), infrastructure refinement (turbolab), and feature richness (dominion-tracker). Most notable: omniMux solidified its offline-first philosophy with transparent state caching between visits, while dominion-tracker's BigPicture feature evolved from a simple browser into a full-featured UI with parallax animations and ambient context. turbolab landed chain-of-thought prompting with self-consistency sampling—a significant capability upgrade for the AI backend. Blopple's test coverage work continues the TDD-first commitment, extracting and verifying complex systems (map migrations, pathfinding, combat) before they rot.

## Per-Repo Activity

### omniMux
Invested in local-first resilience: search results now cache between visits, the library persists across sessions, and scroll position restores when you return to a page. Added light theme support. These changes operationalize the offline-first principle—the app now remembers your context without touching the network, matching the philosophy of reducing cloud dependency.

### Blopple
Test coverage expansion across three critical systems: pathfinding, combat, and engine bounds now have real test suites, and map migrations (the most fragile upgrade path) were extracted into their own module with 422 lines of test coverage. Fixed rejection handling in audio playback and pointer lock to fail closed rather than silently. Added map JSON schema validation at load time. The TypeScript and lint toolchain was wired up, bringing the project's CI surface into the testing harness.

### turbolab
Landed Chain-of-Thought prompting with self-consistency sampling—the ability to generate multiple reasoning paths and vote on consistency. Added a configurable default system prompt so users aren't stuck with hardcoded defaults. Squeezed performance: cache reuse, larger prefill batches, physical core threading, and bumped proxy header timeout to 15 minutes for long-running inferences. Bug fixes around GGUF auto-detection and cross-device updates cleaned up rough edges in the model loading pipeline.

### dominion-tracker
BigPicture matured from a basic browser into a polished UI feature: a cover-flow launcher with parallax scrolling, spring animations, and reactive ambient visuals. Supports remote-friendly build creation and sorting players by games played. Added Dark Ages expansion and Shelters toggle for Dominion variants. Non-participants can now comment on live games, opening the social surface. Docker image cleanup removed bundled package managers to shrink the runtime footprint.

### vitalSVG
Footer link to the project repository.

### refundesk
New project initialized with boilerplate.

1. `## Summary` — what shipped, what you were deep in, anything notable across repos

completion:
## Summary

Across five active projects, the week split between shipping user-facing features and infrastructure hardening. **init-launcher** got a runtime theme system and UI polish. **dominion-tracker** launched its BigPicture builds browser with ambient cover-flow UX. **turbolab** added release signature verification. **fanoutd** matured its planning agent with streaming progress and transient retry logic. **Blopple** shipped standalone HTML export and editor polish (undo/redo, aspect-preserving fullscreen). The pattern across these: incremental feature stacking where each commit adds a discrete capability, paired with performance and reliability tuning.

## Per-Repo Activity

### init-launcher
Runtime theme system landed for both launcher and lockscreen, paired with immersive mode (hiding status and nav bars). Added URL action tiles to the pinned grid, expanding what the launcher can pin. Release workflow now builds on tag — the infrastructure to ship binaries automatically.

### dominion-tracker
BigPicture emerged as a major feature: a cover-flow builds browser with reactive ambient, parallax, and spring physics. Builds can be colored by kind (book vs custom). Added clickable back buttons, game cancellation, local dates, and player bios — the polish that makes historical browsing feel native rather than bolted on.

### turbolab
Self-update flow gained signature verification (safety against tampered releases) and clearer error messaging for non-JSON responses. Chat attachments now render as a file list with modal preview instead of inline — better for large or numerous attachments.

### fanoutd
The planning agent layer matured significantly. Now accepts caller-supplied plans (bypassing re-orchestration), streams planning progress to the webui, exposes model and review toggle in the modal. Fixed transient LLM failures by retrying instead of hard-failing. Capped goal verbosity in prompts and removed inter-step sleeps — both helping the agent stay responsive and on-budget.

### Blopple
Standalone HTML export shipped — games can now be saved as a single portable file. Added recent-saves list and export modal to the editor. Texture and tilemap editors now support undo/redo. Mirrored wall/riser textures corrected. Canvas creation optimized with `alpha:false`, and a hot loop (per-row plane distance) hoisted out of the column iteration.

## Summary

A wide span of shipping across the FOSS portfolio: turbolab hardened its update pipeline with signature verification while improving chat UX; omniMux got aggressive with client-side caching and theme support to reduce network friction; dominion-tracker expanded its game catalog and gameplay rules; and init-launcher gained a runtime theme system on Android. The throughput split between polish (caching, theming, error messages) and capability expansion (game content, feature unlock for participants). One new project kickoff (refundesk) and infrastructure work (Docker image cleanup, CI/CD wiring).

## Per-Repo Activity

### turbolab

Added cryptographic signature verification to the self-update flow—release binaries now validate before install, closing a supply-chain gap in the update mechanism. Separately, improved error handling to parse and surface JSON failures instead of dumping raw responses when the release endpoint breaks.

### dominion-tracker

Shipped Dark Ages expansion support with a Shelters toggle and reordered player rankings by games played. Pushed non-participants into the comment flow for live games (removing a gate), and trimmed package managers from the Docker runtime image to shrink attack surface.

### omniMux

Built a three-layer caching system for the web client: search results sticky across navigation, full library cache on revisit, and scroll position restoration per-route. Added light theme support, completing the theme toggle pattern. Collectively, these reduce friction for users who don't want to re-fetch or re-scroll on every page transition.

### refundesk

Initialized a new project with Docker and environment scaffolding.

### init-launcher

Wired a runtime theming system for the Android launcher and lockscreen, then hid system UI bars (status and nav) for a full-immersion presentation mode.

### Blopple

Added itch.io thumbnail asset for distribution.

## Summary

Heavy week across five active repos. **omniMux** absorbed most focus: completed auto-update infrastructure (banner, one-click apply, install script) and shore up deployment ergonomics (secrets to .env, docker-compose tweaks, root warning removal). **dominion-tracker** continued its SQLite migration arc — merged Swiss-pod tournament logic, fixed multi-stage Docker builds for native deps, and redesigned achievements from a tab into inline badges with custom SVG. **socialChat** picked up a couple of bot personality flavors via dependadocs automation. **Blopple** got minor fixes for itch.io HTML5 packaging. **go-course** went live as a new teaching project with lesson structure and landing page.

## Per-Repo Activity

### usr-wwelsh/go-course
Brand new project initialized with lesson content structure and a landing page. Added favicon and social preview card for web presence — typical setup for a teaching resource.

### usr-wwelsh/omniMux
Auto-update feature landed after several iterations: settings toggle, install script, opt-in banner with one-click apply, and changelog display. Concurrent deployment fixes tackled secrets management (migrated from toggles to .env), docker-compose cleanup, and removed spurious root warnings. Also wired up QuickJS and Android VR media handling.

### usr-wwelsh/socialChat
Merged two rounds of dependadocs-driven dependency updates, and added two new bot personalities (`just_use_xgboost`, `agent_maxxer_9000`) — fun domain-specific flavor additions to the bot roster.

Minor fixes for itch.io HTML5 export: relative asset paths to avoid hardcoded absolute references, and map-gen logic to keep exit tiles away from player start position.

### usr-wwelsh/dominion-tracker
Season 2 rewrite continues: merged Swiss-pod tournament port to SQLite, fixed multi-stage Docker builds for native module compilation, and redesigned achievements UI (moved from separate tab to inline under stats with custom SVG badges). Also added a one-shot Postgres→SQLite recovery script and trivy CVE ignore rule for unpatchable base-image vulns.

Five active projects across the week. **dominion-tracker** saw the largest push — a new builds browser emerged from the bigpicture module, complete with reactive UI animations and remote-friendly scaffolding. **cde-wallpaper** gained CLI scripting support; **turbolab** hardened process recovery for the llama-server backend; **socialChat** closed a security hole in bot auth. ## Per-Repo Activity

### cde-wallpaper
CLI interface landed in `cli.rs` — argument parsing and delegation to main. Opens the tool to scripting workflows beyond the GUI.

### turbolab
Process manager now detects broken llama-server instances and re-installs. Improves reliability for the dual-backend inference stack.

### dominion-tracker
Dominion tracker exploded. Bigpicture went from a stats view to a full builds browser — color-coded by expansion (book vs. custom), playable launcher with cover-flow navigation and spring-animated parallax, local date handling, player bios, Dark Ages expansion + Shelters toggle. Remote-friendly build creator. This is a substantial UX expansion.

### socialChat
Removed hardcoded bot passwords and made bot accounts unloggable. Closes a surface for credential leakage in the self-hosted social stack.

# Developer Journal — 2026-07-15

## Summary

This week split between feature work on **dominion-tracker** (tournament infrastructure + UI polish), targeted memory debugging in **turbolab** (process lifecycle management), a security hardening in **socialChat** (bot account constraints), and responsive UX fixes scattered across **omniMux** and **Blopple**.

The standout theme: tournament and build tooling on dominion-tracker matured significantly. Swiss pod mode, build ratings, and a polished cover-flow launcher moved the project from demo toward usable. Meanwhile, turbolab hit a real production issue—unbounded memory growth in the embedding server—and got a targeted fix with process recycling, rather than a full architectural rework. That's the pragmatic move: identify the leak, isolate the flags, recycle the process when RAM caps. socialChat got a quiet security win: bot accounts now refuse login attempts and dropped hardcoded passwords entirely, shrinking the attack surface without visible UX impact.

## Per-Repo Activity

### dominion-tracker
Swiss tournament mode landed in the backend (migrations + route handlers), paired with UI work for the big-picture tournament view and a new builds browser. Star ratings for builds give players feedback on deck quality. The visual polish—cover-flow launcher with parallax and spring animations, color-coding builds by source (book vs custom), clickable back buttons—suggests the project is moving from "can track games" to "enjoyable to use." ~600 lines of new frontend code in one commit; refactoring stayed minimal, letting feature work land fast.

### turbolab
Process memory management got scrutiny after embedding server processes grew unbounded. Three commits in close sequence: first debug logging, then flag isolation (embedding servers were inheriting parent flags), finally a recycler that automatically restarts processes when they exceed memory thresholds. The solution avoids rewriting the process manager; instead it monitors and recovers. The actual fix was small (6 lines in manager.go + config hook), but the diagnostic work was deliberate.

### socialChat
Bot account hardening: removed login logic for bot-created accounts (they can't authenticate now) and stripped hardcoded passwords from the bot service. Minimal diff, maximum security impact. The bot service now only uses env-based secrets or session mechanisms, closing a class of credential exposure.

### omniMux
Responsive grid layout fixes for mobile: album and playlist grids now reflow properly on narrow phone screens. Targeted CSS changes; no data model shifts.

### Blopple
Image import got crop, zoom, and chroma-key background removal in a single feature commit. The new ImageImportModal is substantial (~360 lines), suggesting first-class image editing is now baked into texture workflows rather than deferred to external tools.

## Summary

A broad sweep across the portfolio this week: **Blopple** shipped combat fundamentals (weapons, pickups, keys/doors), **go-course** wired certificates into LinkedIn's social graph, **vitalSVG** hardened against rate abuse and DOM injection, and **init-launcher** added mobile device vitals to the lockscreen. The arc shows movement from building blocks (tooling, infrastructure) to user-facing features that bridge into adjacent systems.

## Per-Repo Activity

### go-course
Surfaced completion certificates as a social artifact — added a downloadable cert with LinkedIn share integration, then made the sharing link unique and persistent. The redirect point (on `certificate.ts`) suggests treating proof-of-completion as a URL-first asset rather than a modal dump.

### Blopple
Rounding out the game editor's runtime. Shipped weapon/pickup/equip mechanics and door locks keyed by colored keys; fixed a spawnpoint bug (exit tiles were landing too close to the player). Also patched asset paths for itch.io deployment, moving from a dev-only assumption to cross-platform delivery. The roadmap additions (weapons as reskin templates, multilevel support) signal what the editor's future conversation will be about.

### omniMux
Added light mode. Simple feature, meaningful for a music app that people use in daylight.

### refundesk
Project initialized — the Dockerfile and .env.example suggest this is headed toward a containerized service. Nothing shipped yet, just the skeleton.

### dominion-tracker
Pulled in a Dependadocs update via merge. Maintenance, not new work.

### init-launcher
Wired battery state (percentage + charging status) into the lockscreen. Low-level device telemetry that makes the lockscreen more useful without opening the phone.

### vitalSVG
Addressed two classes of risk: added per-IP rate limiting to stop abuse (returning 429), and fixed a DOM injection vulnerability where untrusted resource names could inject into the UI. Rate limiting is the kind of work that doesn't ship as a feature but prevents shipping *without* it.

# Developer Journal — 2026-08-20 to 2026-08-24

## Summary

This week was split between stabilization work on two mature projects and infrastructure for new ones. **dominion-tracker** saw a significant migration challenge: recovering from a Postgres production failure and shipping a parallel SQLite-based tournament system in the same window. **omniMux** reached a polish milestone with stateful caching across page visits—search history, library, scroll position—turning a volatile web app into one that feels like it remembers you. Both got Docker/deployment fixes that unblock their CI. Two new projects—go-course and refundesk—were scaffolded with just enough structure to start.

## Per-Repo Activity

### dominion-tracker

Heavy week oscillating between crisis and feature. A Postgres failure triggered a one-shot recovery script (`recover-from-postgres.sh`) and manual GitHub workflow, then pivoted into porting Swiss-pod tournaments to SQLite as part of season-2 migration. Parallel work added Dark Ages expansion support and achievement badge visuals (custom SVG icons for milestones). Docker multi-stage build fixed better-sqlite3 compilation from source, a blocker for CI. The Trivy CVE ignore pragmatically unblocks deploys from unfixable base-image vulnerabilities.

### omniMux

Three related features completed this window—search result caching, library caching, and scroll-position restoration—each backed by test suites. They're modest individually but compound into a materially better experience: leave the library and come back, your scroll is restored; search, navigate away, return and your results are still there. Light theme landed alongside settings UI cleanup (JWT_SECRET docs, removed redundant toggles). Auto-update banner with changelog went in earlier in the week, surfacing more gracefully than silent background upgrades would.

### go-course

Skeleton shipped: lesson structure, starter code template, favicon, and social preview card. Ready for lesson authoring.

### socialChat

Two new bot personalities (just_use_xgboost, agent_maxxer_9000) for variety. Dependadocs PRs merged from scheduled runs.

### Blopple

Two small fixes: exit tile now positions away from player start in the editor, and asset paths went relative for itch.io HTML5 deployment.

### refundesk

New project initialized with boilerplate (Dockerfile, .env template, Flask app structure). Blank canvas mode.

## Summary

A productive week across the portfolio. Two new projects initialized while existing repos absorbed significant feature work: Blopple absorbed a test-coverage push with migration extraction and image-editing polish; turbolab jumped forward on sampling strategies and prompt configuration; dominion-tracker built out a "big picture" interface with build browsing and ratings; omniMux added light-mode support and hardened cover-art fetching under load.

The pattern reads as "breadth with discipline"—six active repos, but each change tied to a clear behavior (new test, validated input, retried fetch, etc.) rather than speculative infrastructure. Worth noting: the test harness in Blopple is now thick enough to drive refactoring directly (`pathfinding.test.ts`, `migrateMap.test.ts`), and turbolab's chain-of-thought work suggests the model-serving layer is moving toward inference-time reasoning, not just prompt templates.

## Per-Repo Activity

### Blopple

Test-first payoff: extracted the map migration chain into its own module and covered it with 422 lines of test cases *before* moving the code. Separately, validation and audio/input error handling got hardened against rejected promises. The repo's test suite now covers pathfinding, combat, engine bounds, and legacy map structures—tight enough to make dead-code removal (unused render params, shadowed loop vars) safe.

### dominion-tracker

Shipped a "big picture" feature: reactive cover-flow launcher with parallax and spring physics, plus a builds browser with filtering, ratings (1-5 stars), and kind-based color coding (book vs. custom builds). Paired with schema work (new `build_ratings` table). The interface serves the use case of reviewing past games and comparing build patterns without navigating individual game records.

### git-digest

New project. A Go CLI tool for curating Git history—initial commit includes the main binary and MIT license. Suggests an experiment in digesting/summarizing repos programmatically.

### go-course

Shipping phase for a completion certificate. Added downloadable cert generation with LinkedIn add-to-profile integration and a shareable, unique URL per user. The certificate infrastructure (TypeScript + storage) sits between the course UI and social-proof workflows.

### omniMux

Light-mode support added to the web player, paired with UX fixes: drop shadows on fullscreen buttons for contrast over album art, lazy-loaded art with fallback handling. API layer now meters and retries cover-art requests to Navidrome (119 lines of test coverage for the proxy). Protects against thundering-herd when album art is missing or slow.

### turbolab

Chain-of-thought prompting and self-consistency sampling landed—152 lines of CoT orchestration plus 188 lines of test coverage for candidate generation and voting. Also: configurable default system prompt, update/cross-device fixes, GGUF detection fix, and prefill-batch tuning. The sampling feature lets users see internal reasoning branches, not just final answers.

### vitalSVG

Footer link to project source—minimal, polish-level change.

### refundesk

New project initialized. Dockerfile, env template, Python app structure. No clear signal yet on the surface; structure suggests a web service.
